name: smallcase
tagline: B2B2C platform for model portfolios of stocks and ETFs via brokers
facts: 2015, Bengaluru; Vasanth Kamath, Anugrah Shrivastava, Rohan Gupta
Private; Peak XV largest external holder (~16%)

strategy.label: Mission
strategy.text: Make thematic, rules-based portfolio investing simple, transparent and accessible to every Indian investor.

strategy.label: Vision
strategy.text: Become the infrastructure layer for managed portfolios in India across stocks, ETFs, mutual funds and global assets.

strategy.label: Core strategy
strategy.text: B2B2C: plug into brokers via Gateway APIs; investors buy portfolios in their own demat accounts, no new KYC.

strategy.label: Moat
strategy.text: Distribution across most major brokers plus 250+ SEBI-registered managers; two-sided network hard to replicate.

strategy.label: Key bet
strategy.text: Expand product shelf: MF model portfolios, US stocks via GIFT City, loans against mutual funds, fixed income.

strategy.label: Your view
strategy.text: If Zerodha and Groww build in-house baskets, does a broker-dependent B2B2C model keep its distribution?

customers.who: Salaried investors wanting curated stock baskets
customers.pain: Picking and rebalancing stocks is time-consuming and confusing
customers.why: Themed portfolios with one-click rebalance, held in their own demat

customers.pain: Hard to distribute research and execute for retail at scale
customers.why: Ready distribution, subscription billing, execution via partner brokers

customers.who: Zerodha, Groww-style brokers, banks, wealth apps
customers.pain: Need sticky investing products to raise engagement and AUC
customers.why: Plug-and-play Gateway API adds managed portfolios without building them

customers.pain: Selling funds breaks compounding and triggers tax
customers.why: Digital loans against mutual funds, from ~9.99% interest

customers.who: Investors wanting global and multi-asset exposure
customers.pain: Global investing is fragmented and paperwork-heavy
customers.why: US stocks via GIFT City and MF portfolios in one place

portfolio.north_star: Investors holding an active portfolio for 12+ months
portfolio.key_metrics: Subscriptions, AUM in smallcases, rebalance compliance, repeat purchases
portfolio.guardrails: Underperformance vs benchmark, mis-selling complaints, unsubscribe rate

products.desc: APIs letting any app transact via user's broker account

products.name: Publisher platform
products.desc: Tools for managers to create, price and manage smallcases

products.name: Broker integrations
products.desc: Investing inside major partner broker apps and websites

portfolio.north_star: Transaction value flowing through partner integrations
portfolio.key_metrics: Active partners, transactions per partner, API uptime, revenue per broker
portfolio.guardrails: Partner concentration, order failures, data security incidents

rows.who_uses: Investors buying smallcases on broker apps
rows.how: Fee per transaction or share of brokerage; bulk of revenue
Subscription fee split between manager and platform
Subscription fees on paid Windmill smallcases
Distribution commission and processing fees on loans

bullets.label: Revenue mix
bullets.text: Mostly broker transaction fees; subscriptions, research and lending distribution growing. FY26 results not yet public.

bullets.label: Users vs payers
bullets.text: Investors often pay nothing directly; brokers and managers pay to access the investor base.

bullets.label: Unit economics
bullets.text: FY25 EBITDA loss narrowed to ~₹9 cr; asset-light, but revenue depends on market cycle volumes.

bullets.label: Growth levers
bullets.text: New asset classes, more partners, paid manager marketplace, credit, global investing.

bullets.label: Market cycle
bullets.text: SEBI F&O curbs push traders to long-term products; weaker markets since late 2024 hurt volumes.

friction: Users must log in to broker for each order
Rebalance updates ignored, portfolios drift from model
Paid manager quality and returns hard to judge
Minimum investment high for portfolios with pricey stocks
Fragmented experience across many partner broker apps

competitors.label: Broker baskets
competitors.text: Zerodha baskets, Groww, Dhan, Angel One in-house portfolios

competitors.label: Mutual funds / PMS
competitors.text: Index funds, thematic MFs, PMS houses

competitors.label: Advisory
competitors.text: SEBI RIAs on direct platforms, Liquide, Sahi

competitors.label: Edge
competitors.text: Broker-neutral rails plus largest manager network; investors keep own demat

competitors.label: Risk
competitors.text: Broker disintermediation, prolonged losses, market downturn, SEBI advisory rules
